summary: ARGUS is an onboard health assistant for astronauts on long missions such as Mars, where a message to Earth takes up to 20 minutes. It compares each astronaut with their own personal baseline and catches the “blind spot”: the gap between how they feel and what their sleep, reaction time and heart rate variability show. When someone is impaired or a solar storm is coming, ARGUS proposes safer schedules and shows the risk of each, so the astronaut can notice the change, evaluate it and act on board.
details: A telemetry simulator streams vitals, sleep, check-ins and cabin CO2 into a Spring Boot core with PostgreSQL; a React web app shows the crew live. Each metric is compared with a robust personal baseline (median and MAD over 14 days, excluding the last 3). Six health areas get a normal/watch/act status and one recommended action. A Google OR-Tools CP-SAT solver builds up to three new schedules that respect hard safety rules, and a Monte Carlo simulation tests every plan on the same 2,000 storm scenarios. Goal: help astronauts act on their health without waiting for Earth. Tools: Java 21, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, OR-Tools, React, TypeScript, Docker.
